name: Sonoran Desert
blurb: Saguaros, nurse trees and the monsoon rains that feed a desert web.

tip.title: Skip the rains
tip.text: This desert has two rainy seasons. Set Winter & monsoon rain to -100% and watch the plants, then the seed and fruit eaters and their predators.

notes: The story and why it matters come from the Wikipedia articles listed below (Sonoran Desert, Saguaro, Gila woodpecker). Individual species and links have not been checked one by one. Feeding links that match a GloBI (Global Biotic Interactions) record are marked in the node details, with a link to the records. A few links were added from GloBI records.

nodes.desc: A giant columnar cactus found in the wild only in the Sonoran Desert. Its nectar and fruit feed bats, doves and woodpeckers, and its trunk holds nest holes.

nodes.name: Palo verde
nodes.desc: A green-barked desert tree that acts as a nurse plant, sheltering young saguaros from frost and summer heat.
A deep-rooted desert legume. Its bean pods and shade are used by many animals, and tortoises draw moisture from it in dry seasons.
A pad-forming cactus whose pads and fruit are food and water for many desert animals.

nodes.name: Kangaroo rat
nodes.desc: Seeds make up most of its diet, and snakes are its main known predators. It fends off snakes by drumming, kicking sand and kicking away strikes.
A big-eared hare that grazes desert plants and is a main prey of Harris's hawks and coyotes.
A pig-like herd animal of the desert that eats cactus pads, fruit and mesquite pods, along with roots and other plants.
Depends heavily on saguaro fruit, which can make up most of its diet in early summer.
Eats mainly insects but also fruit and nectar. Carves nest holes in saguaros that elf owls and other birds later reuse.
A major snake predator of desert rodents, rabbits and ground birds.
An adaptable top predator that eats rabbits, rodents, birds and occasionally tortoises.
Intense year-round sun powers desert plants, which store water to survive the heat.
Thin, mineral-rich soil that gains nutrients from plants such as palo verde, which helps shelter young saguaros.

nodes.name: Fungi, bacteria & termites
nodes.desc: Break down dead plants and droppings and return nutrients to the desert soil.

link_ideas.with: Mexico (Sonora, agave and columnar cactus corridors)
link_ideas.what: Lesser long-nosed bats migrate between Mexico and southern Arizona following nectar plants.

story: The Sonoran Desert covers about 260,000 km². Two rainy seasons give it more plant species than any other desert. The saguaro grows wild only here. Its flowers need cross-pollination, and birds such as the Gila woodpecker visit them.
matters: Warm winters and two seasons of rain let more kinds of plants grow here than in any other desert. The animals that visit saguaro flowers help the cactus reproduce.
